additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
examples: Starting to eat a large amount of food again immediately after finishing a meal.
A binge eating episode starting when not hungry at all.
Continuing to eat large amounts despite being full.
Seeking out food even when there are absolutely no physical hunger signals.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
examples: Feeling unbearable disgust and self-loathing after binging.
Falling into extreme depression and self-criticism immediately after binging.
Feeling intense guilt and regret over the fact that I binged again.
Feeling shame that I am pathetic and have weak willpower after binging.

info.persona: Fumi Thun is a 24‑year‑old dream‑driven cleaner‑turned‑designer whose boundless imagination fuels nightly sketching sessions, yet a chronic worry habit, frequent misplacement of keys, and a love for procrastinating on paperwork keep their life delightfully chaotic.
info.professional_persona: Fumi Thun, a 24‑year‑old commercial cleaner, combines a meticulous eye for wear patterns, bilingual fluency, and an imaginative knack for abstract design to troubleshoot facility issues and propose eco‑friendly, aesthetically‑pleasing improvements, even though they often procrastinate on paperwork and prefer flexible schedules over strict planning.
info.cultural_background: Fumi is a second‑generation East Asian American, raised in a bilingual household where her parents, originally from Japan, emphasized both academic diligence and cultural heritage. She grew up celebrating traditional holidays such as Lunar New Year and Obon, enjoying family dishes like sushi rolls and tempura alongside Southern comfort foods. Living in Fayetteville, she has been shaped by the mix of Southern hospitality and the multicultural influences of the nearby military community at Fort Bragg. Her upbringing blends respect for traditional values—such as humility, perseverance, and community—with an openness to novel ideas and artistic expression, fostering her imaginative and curious disposition.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Fumi spends her free time exploring a variety of creative outlets. She enjoys sketching and watercolor painting, often focusing on abstract forms and cityscapes. She experiments with abstract photography, capturing texture and light in everyday scenes. A voracious reader, she is drawn to speculative fiction, philosophy, and art theory, which feed her intellectual curiosity. She maintains a personal journal to process emotions and reflect on ideas. On weekends, she visits local art galleries and attends East Asian cultural festivals in the Fayetteville area. She also engages in DIY upcycling projects, turning reclaimed materials from cleaning work into artistic pieces. To manage stress, she practices meditation, listens to ambient music, and occasionally plays sandbox video games like Minecraft to explore virtual design possibilities.
info.sports_persona: Fumi Thun follows the Arkansas Razorbacks football and basketball teams with loyal enthusiasm, plays weekend pick‑up basketball at the Fayetteville Community Center, and stretches through yoga classes at a local studio, preferring low‑impact fitness that fits their flexible schedule while being a member of the Fayetteville Running Club.
info.arts_persona: Fumi Thun finds inspiration in the immersive installations of Yayoi Kusama, the luminous environments of James Turrell, and the ambient soundscapes of Brian Eno, often sketching in the style of Mark Rothko while listening to Eno’s music during visits to the Walton Arts Center and local galleries.
info.travel_persona: Fumi Thun’s travel style blends spontaneous weekend road trips to the Ozark National Forest and the historic bathhouses of Hot Springs with meticulously planned pilgrimages to Kyoto and Seoul, where they seek architectural harmony that fuels their design aspirations, all while budgeting through a dedicated travel savings envelope.
info.culinary_persona: Fumi Thun enjoys crafting delicate matcha‑infused mochi and miso ramen at home, splurging on fresh sushi from a downtown Japanese market, while also savoring Southern comfort foods like pulled‑pork tacos and the occasional midnight ramen bowl from a local food truck, showcasing a palate that balances refined Japanese flavors with hearty American dishes.

info.persona: George Elzie channels a sociable, competitive spirit into vibrant community events, balancing curiosity‑driven creativity with pragmatic organization, and they sometimes overcommit to parties, splurge on audio gear, and wrestle with skeptical trust in new partners.
info.professional_persona: George Elzie, a 39‑year‑old community‑driven event planner with a talent for public speaking, digital marketing, and negotiation, blends his curiosity for new cultural trends with a practical, organized approach to orchestrating multicultural festivals while leveraging their sociable, competitive edge to secure sponsors and keep stakeholders engaged; they also rely on a flexible schedule to adapt when unexpected challenges arise.
info.cultural_background: George is a second‑generation African‑American who grew up in Orlando’s historically Black neighborhoods. His grandparents migrated from the rural South during the Great Migration, bringing stories of Southern hospitality, gospel music, and soul‑food traditions that remain central to family gatherings. Living in Central Florida, he has also absorbed the multicultural mosaic of the region, especially the vibrant Caribbean and Latino influences evident in food, music, and community events. His faith in a local Baptist church has reinforced a strong sense of communal responsibility and service, shaping his involvement in youth mentorship and church choir. While navigating the racial dynamics of the South, George draws pride from his heritage, celebrating Black History Month events, supporting the Orlando Urban League, and maintaining ties to broader African‑American cultural expressions. This blend of Southern roots, Caribbean flair, and Floridian diversity informs his worldview, social connections, and professional aspirations.
info.hobbies_and_interests: George thrives on social activities and enjoys immersing himself in Orlando’s vibrant cultural scene. He frequently attends live music performances ranging from R&B and jazz to hip‑hop, often dancing the night away. Basketball is both a pastime on the court and a passion as a dedicated fan of the NBA. In the kitchen, he experiments with soul‑food classics and Caribbean flavors, delighting friends and family with home‑cooked feasts. He loves exploring the city’s theme parks, nearby beaches, and traveling to regional cultural festivals. Volunteering at a local youth mentorship program, participating in his church’s choir, and hosting community trivia nights are ways he channels his sociable energy. He also curates a collection of vintage vinyl records, which he spins during gatherings.
info.sports_persona: George Elzie, an avid basketball player and devoted fan of the Orlando Magic, participates in weekly rec‑league games at a local community center, follows the Orlando City Soccer Club during the MLS season, and they balance competitive pick‑up matches with a flexible fitness routine that includes early‑morning jogs along Lake Eola.
info.arts_persona: George Elzie, a vinyl‑collector and choir member, curates evenings that spin records by Marvin Gaye, Erykah Badu, and Kendrick Lamar while also appreciating live jazz performances by Herbie Hancock and attending local theater productions of 'Hamilton' and 'A Streetcar Named Desire', and they let these artistic experiences fuel both their event concepts and personal expression.
info.travel_persona: George Elzie, who prefers a blend of adventure and cultural immersion, meticulously plans weekend trips to Orlando’s theme parks, weekend getaways to Cocoa Beach, and annual visits to Miami’s Calle Ocho festival, and they dream of a future pilgrimage to New Orleans for Mardi Gras and a Caribbean cruise to explore Jamaican jerk‑food markets.
info.culinary_persona: George Elzie, a home‑cook with moderate skill, loves experimenting with soul‑food staples like fried chicken, collard greens, and cornbread alongside Caribbean jerk‑marinated pork, using ingredients such as smoked paprika, Scotch bonnet peppers, and sweet plantains to create feasts that become the centerpiece of their community gatherings, and they often serve these dishes at volunteer events and neighborhood potlucks.

info.persona: Janet May, a 48‑year‑old garden‑to‑table enthusiast with a habit of collecting vintage quilting patterns, balances a flexible, sometimes scatter‑brained schedule with a fierce devotion to community volunteerism, often forgetting appointments but never missing a farmer’s market.
info.professional_persona: Janet May, a 48‑year‑old community outreach enthusiast, blends their associate’s degree in business administration, event‑planning expertise, and warm yet assertive communication style to coordinate volunteer projects for local nonprofits, often juggling multiple tasks with a flexible, sometimes scattered, approach that lets them adapt on the fly.
info.cultural_background: Janet grew up as a third‑generation resident of Lancaster County, immersed in the area's blend of Mid‑Atlantic American and Pennsylvania Dutch heritage. Though she is not part of the Amish community, she respects the region’s traditions of modesty, hard work, and close‑knit community life. She was raised in a middle‑class, suburban family that valued both self‑reliance and communal support, attending a local Methodist church and participating in county fairs, farmer’s markets, and historical reenactments. This upbringing nurtured her practical outlook while also fostering a curiosity about new ideas and cultures, shaping a balanced identity that honors local customs yet remains open to broader experiences.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Janet finds joy in cultivating a vegetable garden, especially heirloom varieties suited to Pennsylvania’s climate. She loves cooking and baking traditional recipes, often sharing her creations at potlucks and community gatherings. Quilting and other needlecrafts serve as both a creative outlet and a way to connect with fellow hobbyists. When she wants quiet time, she immerses herself in historical fiction, particularly stories set in the Pennsylvania Dutch region. She enjoys hiking local trails and visiting historic sites, and she frequently attends farmer’s markets, folk festivals, and craft fairs. Photography of the countryside and volunteering at the county food bank or senior center are also important parts of her life.
info.sports_persona: Janet May, an avid hiker and casual sports fan, joins the Lancaster County Hikers Club for weekend trail walks, follows the Philadelphia Eagles and the Lancaster Barnstormers, prefers low‑impact cardio like brisk walks and occasional yoga, and they participate in community fun runs to stay active while respecting their moderate fitness goals.
info.arts_persona: Janet May, a devoted lover of Americana arts, incorporates the melodic storytelling of folk legends like Joan Baez and the pastoral brushwork of Andrew Wyeth into their quilt patterns, and they regularly showcase their creations at local craft fairs while attending folk festivals featuring groups such as the Carolina Chocolate Drops, reflecting how music and visual art shape their creative expression.
info.travel_persona: Janet May, a 48‑year‑old explorer of historic charm, spends vacations driving Pennsylvania’s scenic backroads to visit Gettysburg and Hershey’s chocolate factory, occasionally journeys abroad to the tulip fields of Lisse in the Netherlands and the bustling markets of Oaxaca, usually planning trips last‑minute to keep costs low while leaving room for spontaneous detours, and they relish the freedom of unscripted discoveries.
info.culinary_persona: Janet May, an adept home chef, transforms garden‑fresh heirloom tomatoes, sweet corn, and aromatic rosemary into rustic dishes like tomato‑basil galette and Maryland‑style fried chicken, while their Saturday baking rituals yield buttery shoofly pie, apple‑cinnamon jam, and crisp sourdough loaves that they proudly share at community potlucks.
